title: Refuse a chip authorization the issuer has already seen

blocks.text: Your issuer's fraud team found the same chip authorization approved twice, an hour apart, at two different merchants: identical DE 55, identical cryptogram, and the HSM verified both. They want the host to keep its own record of chip counters, and they have already had one complaint from a cardholder whose new card was declined for days after it arrived.
`AtcGuard` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/AtcGuard.java` is called once per chip authorization, after the HSM has checked the cryptogram. Finish the three methods marked `TODO`:

items: `card`: which card the counter belongs to;
`atc`: the counter the card sent in DE 55;
`decide`: the verdict, keeping the record up to date.

blocks.text: The `Verdict` values say what each answer means. About ten lines in total.

cases.says: verified authorizations with rising counters are accepted, for each card, and a failed cryptogram is not
a counter equal to or below the last one verified for the card is a replay, even though its cryptogram verifies
a card is its number and its sequence number, so a replacement card with the same number keeps its own counter
the counter is binary, not BCD, so its bytes are read as a number
only a counter whose cryptogram verified is recorded, so a forged high counter does not lock out the genuine card

origin.section: 18.4. A Valid Cryptogram Proves the Card, Not That the Request Is New

concepts: A verified cryptogram proves the card but not freshness: only the last verified ATC per card catches a replay, recorded only after verification; the card key needs the PAN sequence number, and a failed cryptogram is a decline.
